acceptance: A test proves whether a hung stream blocks interpreter exit; if it does, streams run on threads that cannot block exit or are cancelled cooperatively
State used in finally is initialized before the try, with a test injecting a submit failure
Timeout-branch accounting is race-free and cancelled-before-start streams are not counted as executed, with tests
context: 2026-10-04 throughput adversarial review (develop 8ed0c64e1). Exit-blocking finding is unverified; verify first.
description:
Findings in benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py (develop 8ed0c64e1):
- runner.py:435 uses shutdown(wait=False), but concurrent.futures joins its worker threads at interpreter exit, so the CLI may hang at exit until a stuck query finishes. Plausible from stdlib behavior; not reproduced.
- The finally block (:435-450) uses tentatively_cancelled, outstanding_futures and _record_completed_future, defined after the submit loop (:262-320). An exception during submit raises UnboundLocalError, hiding the real error and losing track of submitted futures.
- In the timeout branch (:375-411), a future that finishes between the done() and running() checks gets a "timed out without starting" error and is then recorded as completed (:165-166). Streams cancelled before starting are counted in streams_executed (:160).
